marks.gloss_en: תנינא אפילו כל שהוא -- the mishna's 'even any amount' is adduced as covering the cobbler's needle
לא, איזמל -- 'any amount' denotes the scalpel, not the cobbler's needle; the citation does not reach the needle
איזמל בהדיא קתני לה -- if 'any amount' already means scalpel, why does the mishna state scalpel explicitly?
פירושי קא מפרש -- the explicit scalpel clause explains what 'any amount' denotes
the mishna's phrase 'even any amount' refers to the scalpel; the later explicit scalpel clause explains the phrase
הכי נמי מסתברא -- if a cobbler's needle were valid under 'any amount', the larger scalpel clause would be superfluous
the scalpel clause is necessary to reject a decree against the hornless scalpel due to the horned one; it is not redundant even if the needle were valid
if the smaller cobbler's needle were valid, explicitly validating a scalpel would appear unnecessary
slaughter with a scalpel is valid when the scalpel has no side protrusions
slaughter with an ordinary needle is invalid because a needle pierces rather than cuts
